Dozens of malicious wallpapers found on Steam Workshop: gamers’ accounts at risk

Securelist (Kaspersky)
2026-06-16 14 use cases 3 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Since late 2025, malware has been spreading rapidly through the Steam Workshop, the gaming platform's built-in service for players to create and share custom content. The attackers are primarily targeting gamers in China and Russia.

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Wallpaper Engine spawning script interpreters or LOLBins from workshop content · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Dozens of malicious wallpapers found on Steam Workshop: gamers’ accounts at risk
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Wallpaper Engine spawning Synaptics.exe or ._cache_GAME1.exe (Steam Workshop wallpaper malware) · [LLM] Trojanized AggregatorHost.dll dropped outside System32 (Steam credential-stealer DLL) · [LLM] IOC hash match — Steam Workshop wallpaper malware MD5 bundle · [LLM] Persistence via Run key referencing Wallpaper Engine / Synaptics / NTRaholic paths · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 callback to Steam Workshop wallpaper campaign infrastructure · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Wallpaper Engine spawning Synaptics.exe or ._cache_GAME1.exe (Steam Workshop wallpaper malware) AIInstallation High
Detects the specific child-process chain described in the Kaspersky writeup where the Wallpaper Engine host binary (wallpaper32/64.exe) launches the malicious Synaptics.exe (DarkKomet) backdoor or the ._cache_GAME1.exe dropper bundled inside compromised Steam Workshop application wallpapers. Both filenames are taken verbatim from the article. Rationale: Article explicitly names 'Synaptics.exe' (DarkKomet family) and '._cache_GAME1.exe' as the dropper pair installed by the malicious wallpaper. Parent process is Wallpaper Engine (wallpaper32/64.exe per reviewer feedback). This combination is unique to the documented Steam Workshop campaign and matches no known benign software. Cross-checked against: • https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/win.dark_komet
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Wallpaper Engine 'application' wallpapers that happen to launch a bundled game named NTRaholic from a non-malicious workshop entry (rare but possible if the Synaptics naming clashes with a legitimate Synaptics touchpad utility located in the same path)
  • Synaptics touchpad driver updater (SynTPEnh.exe / Synaptics.exe) genuinely installed by an OEM in C:\Program Files\Synaptics — distinguishable by signed publisher and parent svchost.exe, not wallpaper32.exe
  • Wallpaper Engine internal cache files matching ._cache_* pattern from non-malicious workshop content (the GAME1.exe suffix is the distinguishing token)
  • Red-team simulation using publicly-published IOCs from the Kaspersky article
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Program Files\Synaptics\" and InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has "Synaptics")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Pull the full process tree for the alert — confirm parent is wallpaper32/64.exe and capture the SHA256 of the child Synaptics.exe / ._cache_GAME1.exe. Compare hash against the 13 MD5 IOC bundle in the article. Check DeviceFileEvents for which workshop subscription ID dropped the file (path under \Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\). 2. CONTAIN: Isolate the host via Defender Live Response, kill wallpaper32/64.exe and Synaptics.exe processes, quarantine the dropped binaries, and force-logout the user's Steam session by rotating the password and revoking sessions via Steam Support. 3. HUNT: Search the org for other downloads from the same Steam Workshop entry, pivot on the SHA256 across DeviceFileEvents, and check DeviceNetworkEvents for the C2 IPs 120.48.156.17 and 202.144.192.29.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wallpaper32.exe","wallpaper64.exe","webwallpaper32.exe","webwallpaper64.exe","wallpaperservice32_c.exe","wallpaperservice64_c.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("Synaptics.exe","_cache_GAME1.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Synaptics.exe","._cache_GAME1.exe","NTRaholic")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, MD5
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(web)?wallpaper(32|64)(_c)?\.exe$" or ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\wallpaperservice(32|64)_c\.exe$"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(Synaptics|_cache_GAME1)\.exe$"
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Synaptics.exe","._cache_GAME1.exe","NTRaholic")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, MD5
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Wallpaper Engine Spawning Steam Workshop Wallpaper Malware Droppers
id: 7b1cd2a8-9e4c-4ef0-9b3a-5a2c3b0d8a11
status: experimental
description: Detects Wallpaper Engine host binary launching Synaptics.exe (DarkKomet) or ._cache_GAME1.exe dropper bundled inside malicious Steam Workshop application wallpapers.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/dozens-of-malicious-wallpapers-found-on-steam-workshop/120186/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1059
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\wallpaper32.exe'
      - '\wallpaper64.exe'
      - '\webwallpaper32.exe'
      - '\webwallpaper64.exe'
      - '\wallpaperservice32_c.exe'
      - '\wallpaperservice64_c.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\Synaptics.exe'
      - '\_cache_GAME1.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\wallpaper32.exe OR *\wallpaper64.exe OR *\webwallpaper32.exe OR *\webwallpaper64.exe OR *\Wallpaper32.exe OR *\Wallpaper64.exe) @Image:(*\Synaptics.exe OR *\synaptics.exe OR *\_cache_GAME1.exe OR *\_cache_game1.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/(web)?wallpaper(32|64)(_c)?\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(Synaptics|_cache_GAME1)\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/Synaptics\.exe|_cache_GAME1\.exe|NTRaholic/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wallpaper32.exe","wallpaper64.exe","webwallpaper32.exe","webwallpaper64.exe") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("Synaptics.exe","_cache_GAME1.exe") OR Processes.process="*._cache_GAME1.exe*" OR Processes.process="*Synaptics.exe*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wallpaper32.exe","wallpaper64.exe","webwallpaper32.exe","webwallpaper64.exe") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("Synaptics.exe","_cache_GAME1.exe") OR Processes.process="*._cache_GAME1.exe*" OR Processes.process="*Synaptics.exe*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Trojanized AggregatorHost.dll dropped outside System32 (Steam credential-stealer DLL) AIInstallation High
The article describes a custom AggregatorHost.dll that impersonates the legitimate Windows system DLL and is used to hijack the Steam session. The genuine file ships only inside %SystemRoot%\System32. Any AggregatorHost.dll written to user-writable locations (Steam directories, Wallpaper Engine workshop subdirs, %TEMP%, %APPDATA%) is an immediate red flag. Rationale: Article: 'installs a custom version of a system library called AggregatorHost.dll with a payload inside' — the malicious DLL impersonates the legit Windows file. Any drop outside System32/SysWOW64/WinSxS is anomalous because Windows never relocates that DLL. High-fidelity name+location anomaly.
ATT&CKT1574.001 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Windows servicing operations (DISM, WUSA) temporarily staging system DLLs in %TEMP%\WinSxS-staging during cumulative updates — distinguishable by parent TiWorker.exe/TrustedInstaller.exe
  • Endpoint imaging tools (SCCM, Intune) restoring System32 contents to a backup directory during repair operations
  • Symbol-server caches where a developer copied the file for debugging into a tools directory
  • Red-team simulation using the public IOC bundle
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TiWorker.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","wusa.exe","DISM.exe")
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Hash the dropped AggregatorHost.dll and compare against the legitimate copy at %SystemRoot%\System32\AggregatorHost.dll (file signing certificate is Microsoft Windows Publisher). Check the dropping process — if InitiatingProcessFileName is wallpaper32/64.exe or a process under \Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\, treat as confirmed. 2. CONTAIN: Isolate the host, kill any process with that DLL mapped (use DeviceImageLoadEvents pivot), quarantine the file, and rotate the user's Steam credentials and active session tokens. 3. HUNT: Pivot the DLL SHA256 across the fleet and look for outbound traffic to 120.48.156.17/ey.php — the trojanized DLL exfils Steam session data to that endpoint.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName =~ "AggregatorHost.dll"
| where not (FolderPath has_any (@"\Windows\System32\", @"\Windows\SysWOW64\", @"\Windows\WinSxS\"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName =~ "AggregatorHost.dll"
| where not (TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Windows\System32\", @"\Windows\SysWOW64\", @"\Windows\WinSxS\"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileMD5, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

C2 callback to Steam Workshop wallpaper campaign infrastructure AICommand & Control Medium
Detects outbound connections to the two C2 endpoints named in the article (120.48.156.17 hosting /ey.php for Steam session exfil, 202.144.192.29 hosting /audit.php and /download2/Themes2.zip) or to the brightly.to domain. Captures both IP literal hits and URL-based requests. Rationale: Article verbatim: 'sends all the collected data to a server controlled by the hackers at hxxp://120.48.156[.]17/ey.php' and the IOC block lists http://202.144.192[.]29/audit.php plus http://202.144.192[.]29/download2/Themes2.zip. brightly.to is in the pre-extracted IOCs. Specific IP+URI pairs make this near-zero FP.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel analyst sandbox detonating the same samples and triggering the same callbacks — should be allow-listed by sandbox hostname
  • Security researcher pivoting on the IOCs via curl/wget for verification — distinguishable by user-agent and originating analyst workstation
  • Internal IP-reputation scanner probing the published IOC bundle as part of validation
  • Stale CTI feed pulling the IOC list via HTTP (the feed processor itself reaches the IPs)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\sandbox\"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Identify the host and InitiatingProcessFileName making the connection. If parent is wallpaper32/64.exe, Synaptics.exe, or any process under a Steam workshop directory, treat as confirmed campaign hit. Pull the matching DeviceProcessEvents 5 minutes either side to reconstruct the chain. 2. CONTAIN: Block 120.48.156.17 and 202.144.192.29 at the egress firewall and DNS sinkhole brightly.to. Isolate the host, rotate the user's Steam credentials, and revoke active Steam Web API tokens. 3. HUNT: Pivot the SHA256 of the calling process across the fleet, hash-match all 13 MD5s from the IOC bundle in DeviceFileEvents over 30d, and check whether the user's Steam account was used to publish any new Workshop entries (campaign self-propagation pattern described in article).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("120.48.156.17","202.144.192.29")
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("ey.php","audit.php","download2/Themes2.zip","brightly.to")
   or RemoteUrl has "120.48.156.17"
   or RemoteUrl has "202.144.192.29"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("120.48.156.17","202.144.192.29")
   or Url has_any ("ey.php","audit.php","download2/Themes2.zip","brightly.to","120.48.156.17","202.144.192.29")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, SrcUsername, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Steam Workshop Wallpaper Campaign C2 Callback
id: 9c8a7b6e-2d4f-4e9a-bb12-7f6e5d4c3b22
status: experimental
description: Outbound traffic to the Kaspersky-published C2 IPs and URLs for the Steam Workshop Wallpaper Engine malware campaign (DarkKomet / Lumma / Vidar distribution).
references:
  - https://securelist.com/dozens-of-malicious-wallpapers-found-on-steam-workshop/120186/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1041
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_ip:
    DestinationIp:
      - '120.48.156.17'
      - '202.144.192.29'
  selection_url:
    DestinationHostname|contains:
      - 'brightly.to'
      - '120.48.156.17'
      - '202.144.192.29'
  condition: selection_ip or selection_url
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender OR linux.syslog) (CIDR(@DestinationIp, 120.48.156.17/32) OR CIDR(@DestinationIp, 202.144.192.29/32) OR @url:(*ey.php* OR *audit.php* OR *Themes2.zip* OR *themes2.zip* OR *brightly.to*))
(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 OR #event_simpleName=DnsRequest)
| RemoteAddressIP4=/^(120\.48\.156\.17|202\.144\.192\.29)$/ OR DomainName=/brightly\.to/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, DomainName, RemotePort], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("120.48.156.17","202.144.192.29") OR All_Traffic.dest_ip IN ("120.48.156.17","202.144.192.29")) by host All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | append [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*120.48.156.17/ey.php*" OR Web.url="*202.144.192.29/audit.php*" OR Web.url="*202.144.192.29/download2/Themes2.zip*" OR Web.url="*brightly.to*") by Web.src Web.url Web.user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("120.48.156.17","202.144.192.29") OR All_Traffic.dest_ip IN ("120.48.156.17","202.144.192.29")) by host All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*120.48.156.17/ey.php*" OR Web.url="*202.144.192.29/audit.php*" OR Web.url="*202.144.192.29/download2/Themes2.zip*" OR Web.url="*brightly.to*") by Web.src Web.url Web.user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
IOC hash match — Steam Workshop wallpaper malware MD5 bundle AIInstallation Medium
Hash-based detection for the 13 MD5s published in the Kaspersky IOC bundle. Catches the binaries across process execution, file creation, and parent-process telemetry — gives broad surface coverage even if the campaign rotates filenames and parent process trees. Rationale: 13 MD5 hashes are verbatim from the article's IOC block. Hashing across DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceFileEvents, and DeviceImageLoadEvents catches the dropper, the DarkKomet payload, the trojanized AggregatorHost.dll, and any future variants reusing the same binaries even if filenames are rotated.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware analyst sandbox executing the samples for triage
  • EDR product itself replaying historical alerts that reference these hashes during testing
  • Threat-intel platform staging the hashes locally for indicator validation
  • Red-team exercise using the published IOC bundle
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Confirm the hit is not from a known sandbox / analyst workstation (check `DeviceInfo.MachineGroup`). Capture file path and parent process tree. 2. CONTAIN: Quarantine the file via Defender Live Response, isolate the host, kill any running processes matching the SHA256, and rotate Steam credentials for the logged-on user. 3. HUNT: Use the SHA256 from this hit to back-trace the dropping process; check if the file came from \steamapps\workshop\content\431960\ (the Wallpaper Engine workshop app ID) — if so, identify the workshop subscription IDs and check fleet-wide for the same downloads.
let MaliciousMD5 = dynamic(["95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068","af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a","c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf","d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da","8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854","b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09","ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1","20965254e29104986e11939decd39549","18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883","0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d","5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355","fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6","74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80"]);
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
     | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
     | where MD5 in (MaliciousMD5) or InitiatingProcessMD5 in (MaliciousMD5)
     | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source="Process", Path=FolderPath, FileName, MD5, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceFileEvents
     | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
     | where MD5 in (MaliciousMD5)
     | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="File", Path=FolderPath, FileName, MD5, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents
     | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
     | where MD5 in (MaliciousMD5)
     | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="ImageLoad", Path=FolderPath, FileName, MD5, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
let MaliciousMD5 = dynamic(["95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068","af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a","c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf","d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da","8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854","b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09","ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1","20965254e29104986e11939decd39549","18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883","0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d","5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355","fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6","74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80"]);
union
  (ImProcessCreate | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where MD5 in (MaliciousMD5) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Source="Process", ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, MD5, SHA256),
  (ImFileEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where TargetFileMD5 in (MaliciousMD5) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Source="File", ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, MD5=TargetFileMD5, SHA256=TargetFileSHA256)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Wallpaper Engine spawning script interpreters or LOLBins from workshop content AIExploitation Medium
Broader hunting query for the 'application wallpaper' execution model described in the article — Wallpaper Engine launches user-supplied executables that may chain to cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe, rundll32.exe, or other interpreters. Application wallpapers from Steam Workshop should never legitimately need a script interpreter; this hunts the entire campaign pattern beyond the specific Synaptics/cache_GAME1 filenames. Rationale: Article: 'Application wallpapers are essentially standalone programs' and 'allows foreign code to be run directly on your computer'. Wallpaper Engine itself has no legitimate need to spawn cmd/powershell/wscript — these parent-child pairs are a clean campaign indicator. Catches variants that don't reuse the Synaptics/_cache_GAME1 names from UC1.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.001 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Wallpaper Engine 'Workshop' page launch invoking rundll32.exe for Windows shell preview thumbnails (rare but possible on first-time workshop browsing)
  • Legitimate scene wallpaper using a small PowerShell helper to query system stats (e.g., custom CPU/GPU monitor widget) — should be allow-listed by SHA256 of the workshop entry
  • Wallpaper Engine config repair launching cmd.exe to flush a corrupted cache
  • Steam Big Picture mode launching wallpaper through a shell wrapper
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--update-check","--repair-cache","thumbnail"))
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Pull the full command line — if it contains base64-encoded PowerShell, references a URL, or drops anything to %TEMP%/%APPDATA%, treat as confirmed. Hash the parent .exe (the workshop application wallpaper) and check against the IOC bundle. 2. CONTAIN: Suspend wallpaper32/64.exe, kill child processes, isolate host, snapshot \Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\ subscription directories for forensic analysis. 3. HUNT: Identify the workshop subscription ID and check whether other users in the org downloaded the same wallpaper — pivot on the workshop folder GUID across DeviceFileEvents.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wallpaper32.exe","wallpaper64.exe","webwallpaper32.exe","webwallpaper64.exe","wallpaperservice32_c.exe","wallpaperservice64_c.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
   or (FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\Users\Public\") and FileName endswith ".exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, MD5
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(web)?wallpaper(32|64)(_c)?\.exe$" or ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\wallpaperservice(32|64)_c\.exe$"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|bitsadmin|certutil|curl|wget)\.exe$"
   or ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(AppData\\Local\\Temp|AppData\\Roaming|Users\\Public)\\[^\\]+\.exe$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Wallpaper Engine Spawning Script Interpreter or LOLBin
id: 2f8d4e3a-6b1c-4a9f-92c5-8e3d1f7b6a44
status: experimental
description: Wallpaper Engine application/scene wallpaper executes a Windows script interpreter or LOLBin. Application wallpapers from Steam Workshop should never legitimately require these binaries.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/dozens-of-malicious-wallpapers-found-on-steam-workshop/120186/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1059.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\wallpaper32.exe'
      - '\wallpaper64.exe'
      - '\webwallpaper32.exe'
      - '\webwallpaper64.exe'
      - '\wallpaperservice32_c.exe'
      - '\wallpaperservice64_c.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\wallpaper32.exe OR *\wallpaper64.exe OR *\webwallpaper32.exe OR *\webwallpaper64.exe OR *\Wallpaper32.exe OR *\Wallpaper64.exe) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\CMD.EXE)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/(web)?wallpaper(32|64)(_c)?\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|bitsadmin|certutil|curl|wget)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wallpaper32.exe","wallpaper64.exe","webwallpaper32.exe","webwallpaper64.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wallpaper32.exe","wallpaper64.exe","webwallpaper32.exe","webwallpaper64.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Persistence via Run key referencing Wallpaper Engine / Synaptics / NTRaholic paths AIInstallation Medium
Detects autostart registry writes (Run / RunOnce / Image File Execution Options) that reference the artifacts named in the Kaspersky article — Synaptics.exe outside the legit Synaptics folder, ._cache_GAME1.exe, or any value pointing into \steamapps\workshop\content\431960\ (Wallpaper Engine's workshop directory). DarkKomet's classic Run-key persistence anchored to this campaign's specific filenames. Rationale: Article: 'leave the victim's system infected with backdoors or crypto miners' — backdoors persist. DarkKomet's documented behavior is Run-key persistence, and the article names Synaptics.exe and ._cache_GAME1.exe as the dropped artifacts. Filtering out the legitimate Synaptics touchpad driver path keeps FP rate low.
ATT&CKT1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine Synaptics touchpad driver Run key (HKCU\...\Run\SynTPEnh) — excluded by the \Program Files\Synaptics\ path filter
  • Steam itself registering a Run key referencing steamapps directory for game updaters
  • Wallpaper Engine adding its own Run key during install (under \Wallpaper Engine\wallpaper32.exe, NOT under \workshop\content\)
  • User manually adding NTRaholic to startup after legitimately installing the game from another source
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("steam.exe","steamservice.exe") or RegistryValueData !has @"\steamapps\common\"
Response runbook
1. TRIAGE: Inspect the InitiatingProcessFileName that wrote the registry value — if it's wallpaper32/64.exe, Synaptics.exe (outside the legit Synaptics directory), or ._cache_GAME1.exe, treat as confirmed. Capture the value data path and verify the binary exists. 2. CONTAIN: Delete the registry value, quarantine the file at the referenced path, kill any running instances, and isolate the host. Rotate the user's Steam password and revoke active sessions. 3. HUNT: Pivot the file SHA256 across DeviceProcessEvents to find first execution, check DeviceNetworkEvents for 120.48.156.17/202.144.192.29 callbacks, and hash-match all 13 IOCs across the fleet to find other infected endpoints.
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce", @"\Image File Execution Options\", @"\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\Shell", @"\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\Userinit")
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("Synaptics.exe","_cache_GAME1.exe","NTRaholic",@"\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\")
| where not (RegistryValueData has @"\Program Files\Synaptics\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce", @"\Image File Execution Options\", @"\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\Shell", @"\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\Userinit")
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("Synaptics.exe","_cache_GAME1.exe","NTRaholic",@"\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\")
| where not (RegistryValueData has @"\Program Files\Synaptics\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Run Key Persistence Referencing Steam Workshop Wallpaper Malware Artifacts
id: 6a3f9c1d-4e8b-4d7f-b0a2-9c1d2e5f8b77
status: experimental
description: Autostart registry value written that references Synaptics.exe (outside legit Synaptics path), ._cache_GAME1.exe, NTRaholic, or the Wallpaper Engine workshop content directory.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/dozens-of-malicious-wallpapers-found-on-steam-workshop/120186/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.t1547.001
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_key:
    TargetObject|contains:
      - '\CurrentVersion\Run\'
      - '\CurrentVersion\RunOnce\'
      - '\Image File Execution Options\'
      - '\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\Shell'
      - '\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\Userinit'
  selection_data:
    Details|contains:
      - 'Synaptics.exe'
      - '_cache_GAME1.exe'
      - 'NTRaholic'
      - '\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\'
  filter_legit_synaptics:
    Details|contains: '\Program Files\Synaptics\'
  condition: selection_key and selection_data and not filter_legit_synaptics
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\CurrentVersion\Run\* OR *\CurrentVersion\RunOnce\* OR *\Image File Execution Options\* OR *\currentversion\run\* OR *\currentversion\runonce\*) @Details:(*Synaptics.exe* OR *synaptics.exe* OR *_cache_GAME1.exe* OR *_cache_game1.exe* OR *NTRaholic* OR *ntraholic* OR *\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\*) -@Details:(*\Program Files\Synaptics\* OR *\program files\synaptics\*)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| RegObjectName=/\\CurrentVersion\\(Run|RunOnce)\\|\\Image File Execution Options\\|\\Winlogon\\(Shell|Userinit)/i
| RegStringValue=/Synaptics\.exe|_cache_GAME1\.exe|NTRaholic|\\steamapps\\workshop\\content\\431960\\/i
| NOT RegStringValue=/\\Program Files\\Synaptics\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RegObjectName, RegValueName, RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path IN ("*\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\*","*\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce\\*","*\\CurrentVersion\\Image File Execution Options\\*") AND (Registry.registry_value_data="*Synaptics.exe*" OR Registry.registry_value_data="*_cache_GAME1.exe*" OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\\steamapps\\workshop\\content\\431960\\*" OR Registry.registry_value_data="*NTRaholic*") by host Registry.user Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data Registry.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path IN ("*\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\*","*\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce\\*","*\\CurrentVersion\\Image File Execution Options\\*") AND (Registry.registry_value_data="*Synaptics.exe*" OR Registry.registry_value_data="*_cache_GAME1.exe*" OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\\steamapps\\workshop\\content\\431960\\*" OR Registry.registry_value_data="*NTRaholic*") by host Registry.user Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data Registry.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("202.144.192.29", "120.48.156.17") or RemoteUrl has_any ("brightly.to")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["202.144.192.29", "120.48.156.17"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["brightly.to"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")

ImFileEvent

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows

        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:

level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or SHA1 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or MD5 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or SHA1 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or MD5 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Article-specific behavioural hunt — Dozens of malicious wallpapers found on Steam Workshop: gamers’ accounts at risk Exploitation High
Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Dozens of malicious wallpapers found on Steam Workshop: gamers’ accounts at risk
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("synaptics.exe", "._cache_game1.exe", "aggregatorhost.dll"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")

SprySOCKS Windows C2 egress to FishMonger infrastructure 207.148.78.36 / 207.148.75.122 AICommand & Control Medium
Detects outbound TCP/UDP connections from Windows endpoints to the hardcoded C&C IPs used by SprySOCKS WIN_DRV/WIN_PLUS variants. Article-specific because these are operator-controlled Vultr IPs baked into the backdoor's compiled configuration, not crawled telemetry. Rationale: Direct match on the two hardcoded C2 IPs (207.148.78.36 / 207.148.75.122) ESET published. These are operator-controlled Vultr addresses baked into the WIN_DRV/WIN_PLUS samples — no legitimate enterprise traffic should reach them. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1033/ • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/23/i/earth-lusca-employs-new-linux-backdoor.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1095
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / threat-intel team intentionally connecting to the IPs from a sandbox VM
  • Outbound NAT IP collisions if a corporate proxy briefly shared a /24 with Vultr
  • Vulnerability scanners targeting the IPs from a known-scanner host
  • Network device sending NetFlow/syslog through a Vultr-hosted aggregator
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("207.148.78.36","207.148.75.122")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull DeviceNetworkEvents around the hit and identify the InitiatingProcessFileName + folder path; check whether the binary is signed and whether parent is a service host or anomalous LOLBin. 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender MDE Machine Isolation, block both C2 IPs at the perimeter, capture memory and the binary for hash submission. 3) Hunt: pivot on the binary SHA256 across DeviceProcessEvents and DeviceFileEvents for the last 90 days; query DeviceRegistryEvents for new Services keys created by the same process; review DeviceLogonEvents for the user account around the C2 callback.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("207.148.78.36", "207.148.75.122")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let cc_ips = dynamic(["207.148.78.36", "207.148.75.122"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DestinationIP in (cc_ips)
        | project TimeGenerated, SrcHost = SourceHostName, SrcIP = SourceIP, DstIP = DestinationIP, DstPort = DestinationPort, Proto = Protocol, App = DeviceProduct),
    (ImNetworkSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DstIpAddr in (cc_ips)
        | project TimeGenerated, SrcHost = SrcHostname, SrcIP = SrcIpAddr, DstIP = DstIpAddr, DstPort = DstPortNumber, Proto = NetworkProtocol, App = EventProduct)
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

WIN_DRV kernel driver service installed from non-system path AIInstallation High
SprySOCKS WIN_DRV loads a kernel driver to hide processes, files, registry keys and network connections. Detects service installation events (EID 7045 / 4697) where service type indicates a kernel-mode driver and the image path is outside the canonical Windows driver directories — the article calls out kernel-driver-based rootkit behaviour as the WIN_DRV signature. Rationale: Article specifies WIN_DRV uses kernel drivers to hide network connections, processes, files and registry keys. ServiceType=kernel + non-system path is the install signature. Excluding the four legitimate driver paths keeps FPs to genuinely rare WHQL-bypass or rootkit installs. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1014/
ATT&CKT1543.003 T1014 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Services
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • VPN client installers (Cisco AnyConnect, GlobalProtect) dropping drivers under Program Files
  • Endpoint security tools (CrowdStrike, SentinelOne) installing kernel sensors
  • Virtualisation tooling (VMware Tools, VirtualBox guest additions) installing drivers from vendor folders
  • Hardware vendor drivers (Dell, HP) installed via OEM updater into Program Files\<Vendor>
Suppression filter
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$" | where ServiceFileName !has_any ("\\Program Files\\Cisco\\", "\\Program Files\\CrowdStrike\\", "\\Program Files\\VMware\\", "\\Program Files\\SentinelOne\\", "\\Program Files\\Palo Alto Networks\\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the .sys file, verify Authenticode signer and WHQL status; pull EID 6 (Sysmon driver load) on the same host to confirm load succeeded. 2) Contain: if signer is untrusted or unsigned, isolate the host and submit the driver hash to threat intel; disable the service via Defender Live Response (sc.exe stop / delete). 3) Hunt: search DeviceNetworkEvents from the host for callbacks to 207.148.78.36 / 207.148.75.122; query DeviceFileEvents for the .sys hash across the fleet; check DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities for CVE-2023-24932 exposure on the same hosts.
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("DriverLoad", "ServiceInstalled")
| where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\drivers\"
    and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\SysWOW64\drivers\"
    and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore\"
| where FileName endswith ".sys"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4697
| where ServiceType has "kernel"
| where ServiceFileName !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\drivers\"
    and ServiceFileName !startswith @"\??\C:\Windows\System32\drivers\"
    and ServiceFileName !startswith @"C:\Windows\SysWOW64\drivers\"
    and ServiceFileName !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore\"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ServiceName, ServiceFileName, ServiceType, ServiceStartType, ServiceAccount
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SprySOCKS WIN_DRV / WIN_PLUS binary hash hit on Windows endpoint AIInstallation Medium
Detects execution or write of any of the 11 SHA1 hashes ESET attributes to SprySOCKS WIN_DRV and WIN_PLUS Windows variants. High-fidelity binary-match detection that flags both already-installed implants and fresh drops. Rationale: All 11 SHA1 hashes are pulled directly from the ESET article as confirmed SprySOCKS Windows variant samples. Hash equality is the highest-confidence detection shape — zero ambiguity on intent. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1033/
ATT&CKT1059 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sandbox / malware analyst VM detonating the sample under controlled conditions
  • Threat-intel team intentionally pulling samples for YARA validation
  • Backup/forensics tools (FTK Imager, X-Ways) reading the binary while imaging an infected host's disk
  • Defender/AV file-scan event re-touching a quarantined sample
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("SANDBOX", "MALWARE", "FORENSIC", "-IR-"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm hash via Defender DeviceFileEvents — record DeviceName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, AccountName. Differentiate execution (DeviceProcessEvents) vs dormant on-disk (DeviceFileEvents only). 2) Contain: isolate the host, capture memory + the binary, block the SHA1/SHA256 fleet-wide via Defender custom indicator. 3) Hunt: pivot on Vultr C2 IPs 207.148.78.36 / 207.148.75.122 across DeviceNetworkEvents for the last 90d; review DeviceLogonEvents on the infected host for the user account and check IdentityLogonEvents for lateral pivots; query DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities for CVE-2023-24932 exposure on the same host given possible UEFI bootkit chaining.

    "621D1952839BE4B0A1B0E66E87BCE5062CA368ED",
    "2457EED2AB28E37741F10914EF929DAD2C8079D4",
    "D2C706B1EAF662BF0CE124B5032F73ED84BDA24A",
    "5F3B87CEF56683D9A9E19186E0FD0D8019B559C4",
    "C793CA31E3F6628B5C8986146953BF66232E9A30",
    "037DB2445F3D72388CB2CF8510563148E5A184BE"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(90d)

Boot Manager / BCD tampering indicative of CVE-2023-24932 BlackLotus-style UEFI bootkit AIInstallation Medium
ESET reports limited indications SprySOCKS deployment may chain a UEFI bootkit possibly exploiting CVE-2023-24932 (BlackLotus's Secure Boot bypass). Detects writes to the EFI System Partition boot manager and BCD modifications using bcdedit that are the on-disk signature of bootkit installation. Rationale: ESET explicitly notes possible CVE-2023-24932 (BlackLotus Secure Boot bypass) chaining. The canonical BlackLotus install signature is replacing bootmgfw.efi / bootx64.efi on the EFI system partition, or bcdedit modifying the bootmgr description / path. Excluding TrustedInstaller / MoUsoCoreWorker / setup.exe filters legitimate Windows Update boot manager refresh. Cross-checked against: • https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2023-24932 • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/bootkitty-analyzing-first-uefi-bootkit-linux/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1542/003/
ATT&CKT1542.003 T1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Windows Update KB5025885 / cumulative servicing pass refreshing boot manager outside TrustedInstaller wrapping
  • Dual-boot Linux installation writing to \EFI\Boot\bootx64.efi from a live USB
  • Disk-imaging restore (Veeam / Acronis bare-metal) rewriting EFI partition
  • Manual recovery — admin running bcdedit /set or bootrec /fixboot during repair
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","MoUsoCoreWorker.exe","wuauclt.exe","setup.exe","bcdboot.exe","BootRec.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("services.exe","wininit.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull DeviceFileEvents to identify writing process + parent chain; collect the new .efi binary hash and verify Authenticode against Microsoft signer. Cross-check OS build vs KB5025885 / KB5036896 install state to rule out a real Windows Update servicing pass. 2) Contain: if signer is non-Microsoft or process chain is suspicious, image the disk before reboot (bootkit may persist across OS reinstall), isolate the host, escalate to IR for offline EFI analysis. 3) Hunt: query DeviceNetworkEvents for SprySOCKS C2 (207.148.78.36 / 207.148.75.122) from the same host; check DeviceProcessEvents for any of the 11 SprySOCKS SHA1s; pivot DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities for CVE-2023-24932 unpatched hosts across the fleet.
union isfuzzy=true
    (DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where FolderPath has_any (@"\EFI\Microsoft\Boot\", @"\EFI\Boot\")
            or FileName in~ ("bootmgfw.efi", "bootmgr.efi", "bootx64.efi", "winload.efi")
        | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "MoUsoCoreWorker.exe", "setup.exe", "BootRec.exe", "bcdboot.exe")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName),
    (DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where FileName =~ "bcdedit.exe"
        | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/set", "/copy", "/create")
        | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("bootmgr", "path", "description", "{bootmgr}", "nointegritychecks", "testsigning")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType = "BcdeditExec", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256 = "", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine = ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName = AccountName)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\EFI\Microsoft\Boot\", @"\EFI\Boot\")
            or TargetFileName in~ ("bootmgfw.efi", "bootmgr.efi", "bootx64.efi", "winload.efi")
        | where ActingProcessName !has_any ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "MoUsoCoreWorker.exe", "setup.exe", "BootRec.exe", "bcdboot.exe")
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, Event = "EfiFileWrite", File = TargetFileName, Path = TargetFilePath, Process = ActingProcessName, Cmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, User = ActorUsername),
    (ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where ActingProcessName =~ "bcdedit.exe" or TargetProcessName =~ "bcdedit.exe"
        | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/set", "/copy", "/create")
        | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bootmgr", "path", "description", "{bootmgr}", "nointegritychecks", "testsigning")
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, Event = "BcdeditExec", File = ActingProcessName, Path = "", Process = ParentProcessName, Cmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, User = ActorUsername)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: EFI Boot Manager Tampering (Possible CVE-2023-24932 BlackLotus / SprySOCKS UEFI Chain)
id: 4a8b6c12-7e9d-43f5-bf21-9c8a7d3e4f01
description: Write to the EFI System Partition boot manager binaries by a process other than the legitimate Windows update / setup chain. Consistent with BlackLotus-style UEFI bootkit install possibly chained with SprySOCKS.
references:
    - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/fishmongers-arsenal-upgraded-sprysocks-windows/
    - https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2023-24932
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.defense_evasion
    - attack.t1542.003
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\EFI\Microsoft\Boot\'
            - '\EFI\Boot\'
    selection_name:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\bootmgfw.efi'
            - '\bootmgr.efi'
            - '\bootx64.efi'
            - '\winload.efi'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
            - '\MoUsoCoreWorker.exe'
            - '\setup.exe'
            - '\BootRec.exe'
            - '\bcdboot.exe'
    condition: (selection_path or selection_name) and not filter_legit
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\EFI\\Microsoft\\Boot\\* OR *\\efi\\microsoft\\boot\\* OR *\\EFI\\Boot\\*) OR @TargetFilename:(*\\bootmgfw.efi OR *\\bootmgr.efi OR *\\bootx64.efi OR *\\winload.efi)) -@Image:(*\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\MoUsoCoreWorker.exe OR *\\setup.exe OR *\\BootRec.exe OR *\\bcdboot.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| regex("(?i)\\\\(EFI\\\\Microsoft\\\\Boot\\\\|EFI\\\\Boot\\\\|bootmgfw\\.efi|bootmgr\\.efi|bootx64\\.efi|winload\\.efi)", field=TargetFileName)
| NOT regex("(?i)\\\\(TrustedInstaller|MoUsoCoreWorker|setup|BootRec|bcdboot)\\.exe", field=ContextImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2023-24932")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2023-24932")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("955BFC3DCC867256F9F46A606DEB0779FA3416D8", "44DC4A08C5EB0972C8E18B0E01284E06F09006BB", "AB87B29B6F79487C75CA08D102E79001E536F083", "6490B8E4AADE25A3EE2DA9A47F312DB2122470BC", "E7484C24B88A1A2407A8F09D734F9A993670285B", "621D1952839BE4B0A1B0E66E87BCE5062CA368ED", "2457EED2AB28E37741F10914EF929DAD2C8079D4", "D2C706B1EAF662BF0CE124B5032F73ED84BDA24A", "5F3B87CEF56683D9A9E19186E0FD0D8019B559C4", "C793CA31E3F6628B5C8986146953BF66232E9A30", "037DB2445F3D72388CB2CF8510563148E5A184BE") or SHA1 in~ ("955BFC3DCC867256F9F46A606DEB0779FA3416D8", "44DC4A08C5EB0972C8E18B0E01284E06F09006BB", "AB87B29B6F79487C75CA08D102E79001E536F083", "6490B8E4AADE25A3EE2DA9A47F312DB2122470BC", "E7484C24B88A1A2407A8F09D734F9A993670285B", "621D1952839BE4B0A1B0E66E87BCE5062CA368ED", "2457EED2AB28E37741F10914EF929DAD2C8079D4", "D2C706B1EAF662BF0CE124B5032F73ED84BDA24A", "5F3B87CEF56683D9A9E19186E0FD0D8019B559C4", "C793CA31E3F6628B5C8986146953BF66232E9A30", "037DB2445F3D72388CB2CF8510563148E5A184BE") or MD5 in~ ("955BFC3DCC867256F9F46A606DEB0779FA3416D8", "44DC4A08C5EB0972C8E18B0E01284E06F09006BB", "AB87B29B6F79487C75CA08D102E79001E536F083", "6490B8E4AADE25A3EE2DA9A47F312DB2122470BC", "E7484C24B88A1A2407A8F09D734F9A993670285B", "621D1952839BE4B0A1B0E66E87BCE5062CA368ED", "2457EED2AB28E37741F10914EF929DAD2C8079D4", "D2C706B1EAF662BF0CE124B5032F73ED84BDA24A", "5F3B87CEF56683D9A9E19186E0FD0D8019B559C4", "C793CA31E3F6628B5C8986146953BF66232E9A30", "037DB2445F3D72388CB2CF8510563148E5A184BE")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("955BFC3DCC867256F9F46A606DEB0779FA3416D8", "44DC4A08C5EB0972C8E18B0E01284E06F09006BB", "AB87B29B6F79487C75CA08D102E79001E536F083", "6490B8E4AADE25A3EE2DA9A47F312DB2122470BC", "E7484C24B88A1A2407A8F09D734F9A993670285B", "621D1952839BE4B0A1B0E66E87BCE5062CA368ED", "2457EED2AB28E37741F10914EF929DAD2C8079D4", "D2C706B1EAF662BF0CE124B5032F73ED84BDA24A", "5F3B87CEF56683D9A9E19186E0FD0D8019B559C4", "C793CA31E3F6628B5C8986146953BF66232E9A30", "037DB2445F3D72388CB2CF8510563148E5A184BE") or SHA1 in~ ("955BFC3DCC867256F9F46A606DEB0779FA3416D8", "44DC4A08C5EB0972C8E18B0E01284E06F09006BB", "AB87B29B6F79487C75CA08D102E79001E536F083", "6490B8E4AADE25A3EE2DA9A47F312DB2122470BC", "E7484C24B88A1A2407A8F09D734F9A993670285B", "621D1952839BE4B0A1B0E66E87BCE5062CA368ED", "2457EED2AB28E37741F10914EF929DAD2C8079D4", "D2C706B1EAF662BF0CE124B5032F73ED84BDA24A", "5F3B87CEF56683D9A9E19186E0FD0D8019B559C4", "C793CA31E3F6628B5C8986146953BF66232E9A30", "037DB2445F3D72388CB2CF8510563148E5A184BE") or MD5 in~ ("955BFC3DCC867256F9F46A606DEB0779FA3416D8", "44DC4A08C5EB0972C8E18B0E01284E06F09006BB", "AB87B29B6F79487C75CA08D102E79001E536F083", "6490B8E4AADE25A3EE2DA9A47F312DB2122470BC", "E7484C24B88A1A2407A8F09D734F9A993670285B", "621D1952839BE4B0A1B0E66E87BCE5062CA368ED", "2457EED2AB28E37741F10914EF929DAD2C8079D4", "D2C706B1EAF662BF0CE124B5032F73ED84BDA24A", "5F3B87CEF56683D9A9E19186E0FD0D8019B559C4", "C793CA31E3F6628B5C8986146953BF66232E9A30", "037DB2445F3D72388CB2CF8510563148E5A184BE")

                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["955BFC3DCC867256F9F46A606DEB0779FA3416D8", "44DC4A08C5EB0972C8E18B0E01284E06F09006BB", "AB87B29B6F79487C75CA08D102E79001E536F083", "6490B8E4AADE25A3EE2DA9A47F312DB2122470BC", "E7484C24B88A1A2407A8F09D734F9A993670285B", "621D1952839BE4B0A1B0E66E87BCE5062CA368ED", "2457EED2AB28E37741F10914EF929DAD2C8079D4", "D2C706B1EAF662BF0CE124B5032F73ED84BDA24A", "5F3B87CEF56683D9A9E19186E0FD0D8019B559C4", "C793CA31E3F6628B5C8986146953BF66232E9A30", "037DB2445F3D72388CB2CF8510563148E5A184BE"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
